Added in 0.5.0 with the skill. Two Opus 5.5 rows invert on Sonnet 5.5: the Sonnet 5.5 guide adds crop, zoom or code tools for dense images, where the Opus audit re-tests visual scaffolding, and recommends "Think the problem through before you answer" for JSON reasoning tasks, where the Opus audit considers removing "think carefully". The guide also says Sonnet 5 prompts should perform well without changes and that the Sonnet 5 guide's patterns remain a reasonable starting point, so this skill carries no row re-testing Sonnet 5 tuning. On Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform and Microsoft Foundry, the model-config page says a Sonnet 5 entry or `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL` supplies the model Sonnet 5.5's cyber-flagged requests re-run on, and a Sonnet pin naming Sonnet 5.5 itself leaves the refusal standing, so the audit never proposes removing it. Naming these keeps the auditors from borrowing a finding from the Opus table.

Added in 0.5.0 with the skill. The repository requires every model-behavior claim to cite official Anthropic documentation; the System Card is Anthropic's published document but reports evaluations, not instructions, so its rows are low confidence and their notes cite page and section and say no more than the passage does. The maintainer adopted three card-only rows — blanket authorization (p.60–61, §6.2.1), prose-only approval gates (p.69, §6.2.5) and faults copied from replayed history (p.97–98, §7.2.3) — and dropped two: safety language for consumer API products, which is not a Claude Code instruction-surface finding, and a grader told the author is Claude, since the card finds that bias "not measurably different from Claude Sonnet 5's" (p.78–79, §6.3.1) and so not a change of this transition.
